transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-03-26
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~45 mins
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Ramesh (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendez (Head of AI, Marina Logistics), Aisha Khan (Infra Lead), Tom Becker (Procurement)

Summary: quick renewal check-in, discuss committed capacity increase, adding EU and APAC regions, pricing/discounts for a 12-month extension, and next steps to run a short dedicated pilot.
Topics: capacity upgrade, additional regions (EU/APAC), contract extension & discounts, SOC 2/KMS questions, timeline for pilot.

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining - how's it going, Carlos?
[00:06] Carlos: good, thanks. busy quarter but excited to chat through the renewal. we talked internally about bumping our reserved capacity and adding the EU region, maybe APAC later.
[00:16] Priya: hi all - from SE side i'll focus on the technical tradeoffs for dedicated vs hosted for the EU deploy, and the latency numbers we've seen in prior runs.
[00:24] Aisha: quick note, our infra team needs to make sure whatever we do supports our KMS integration and keeps logs within our EU tenancy.
[00:31] Tom: and procurement side - timeline is tight, we want contract terms and pricing this week ideally so we can start the fiscal sign-off.
[00:39] Jordan: got it. high level: you're at 200k tokens/day today on hosted, with seasonal spikes - Carlos, is that still accurate?
[00:47] Carlos: roughly yes, spikes up to 400k for certain routes. we've seen latency at times creep toward 600ms for longer prompts, which has hit our internal SLO.
[00:56] Priya: that aligns with what we saw; continuous batching on hosted helps cost but the latency tail can widen. moving to Dedicated reserved capacity gives a more predictable p99 and lower median in practice, and we can pin model variants.
[01:10] Carlos: how big of a bump do we need? we were thinking about moving to a 2x reserved pool, plus some burst.
[01:16] Jordan: for your current profile, 2x reserved + a small burst buffer is reasonable. i'll send you a pricing comparison for (1) keep hosted + autoscale, (2) 2x Dedicated reserved, (3) 2x Dedicated + burst credits. we'll show cost/year and expected per-token cost.
[01:30] Aisha: EU region - is that private deployment or hosted in EU? we have data residency rules for EU-sourced records.
[01:37] Priya: we have two options: hosted EU region (data at rest in EU and access controls) or Private/VPC deployment where you manage networking and KMS. Hosted EU usually meets most residencies, but for strict legal needs we recommend Private. both support KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs.
[01:52] Carlos: we lean toward hosted EU if it means faster time-to-market - less ops from our side. but if compliance pushes, we'll go private.
[01:59] Tom: for procurement - discount tiers nailed to commitment size? what's typical?
[02:03] Jordan: standard approach: 12-month commit with stepped discounts for higher reserved throughput. i can share a sheet with three tiers. also we can discuss a 60/30/10 billing split for bursts.
[02:13] Carlos: any competitors we should be worried about on price/perf, like OpenAI or Anthropic?
[02:18] Priya: OpenAI is obviously strong on models but latency to EU/APAC can vary; Anthropic similar. AWS SageMaker brings infra control but then you manage more tradeoffs. Redwood positions itself on predictable cost + production tooling (rollouts, KV cache, tracing).
[02:34] Aisha: on the technical pilot - what do you need from our side to spin up a dedicated pool for tests?
[02:40] Priya: ideally: sample traffic replay (anonymized), a handful of representative prompts, and target p99 latency goals. we'll run 2-3 days of throughput tests in EU region and show results.
[02:51] Carlos: we can anonymize and send by EOD tomorrow.
[02:54] Tom: legal question - do you have SOC 2 cert and support for SSO/SAML? we need that to move forward.
[03:00] Jordan: yes SOC 2 Type II, SSO/SAML support, and we have audit logs exposed in the Console. i'll attach the security pack and SOC attestation in the follow-up.
[03:10] Aisha: KMS integration - do you support our cloud KMS (Azure Key Vault)?
[03:14] Priya: yes, we support major KMS providers including AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, and can do HSM for Private. in hosted EU we'd recommend using your tenant KMS for encryption.
[03:24] Carlos: curious about rollback/rollout - if we pin a model and it regresses, how quick to fallback?
[03:29] Priya: Redwood Console supports canary rollouts and automatic fallback to previous variants. if we detect quality drop by your evals, you can auto-failover. latency impact is minimal since kernel selection and KV cache warm-up are considered.
[03:42] Tom: pricing - can you do a mid-year extension with pro-rated discounts if we sign earlier?
[03:47] Jordan: yes we can structure a pro-rated extension to align with your fiscal quarter; i'll include pro-rata options in the quote.
[03:54] Carlos: about APAC - timeline-wise, we'd add APAC after EU, but what's the typical lead time to add a region?
[03:59] Priya: for hosted EU it's immediate once you request, usually a few days to confirm KMS and networking. for APAC it's similar but can take 1-2 weeks for capacity scheduling if you want dedicated GPUs reserved.
[04:11] Carlos: ok. procurement needs a pricing sheet and expected start date so they can queue the PO.
[04:16] Tom: yes, please. also need a sample contract and any minimum termination windows.
[04:21] Jordan: we'll send the pricing, the sample SOW/contract language (12-month + options), and the SOC pack.
[04:27] Aisha: small nit - our prompts sometimes hit 8k tokens; does the Dedicated pool handle longer context well?
[04:33] Priya: yes, runtime supports long sequences, KV cache management, and quantization profiles. for very long context we recommend specific kernel choices we'll note in the benchmark doc.
[04:42] Carlos: any immediate risks we should be aware of?
[04:45] Priya: main risk is under-provisioning for peak traffic; that's why the burst buffer helps. also if you need Private with on-prem there's more lead time.
[04:54] Jordan: to recap - we'll send: committed capacity pricing with tiers, pro-rata extension options, SOC/security pack, and Priya's EU/APAC latency benchmarks in a few days. we'll also schedule the pilot for week of 2026-04-05 pending anonymized traffic.
[05:09] Carlos: sounds good. if we get the quote and legal by Monday we can push to sign.
[05:14] Tom: thanks - can you also list the exact SLA numbers and uptime credits? procurement asks for that.
[05:18] Jordan: yes we'll include SLA table (p99 latency targets, uptime SLA, and credits).
[05:24] Priya: i'll prep a short runbook for the pilot showing required logs, metrics, and the acceptance criteria.
[05:30] Carlos: great, appreciate it.
[05:33] Jordan: thanks everyone - talk soon.

Recap & Next Steps (verbatim):
- Jordan: send committed capacity pricing + pro-rata options, sample SOW, SOC pack (due 2026-03-29).
- Priya: run EU/APAC latency tests and produce benchmark doc + runbook (due 2026-04-02).
- Carlos: share anonymized traffic + confirm regions (due 2026-03-31).
- Tom: share procurement timeline and PO window (due 2026-03-30).

End of transcript.
